Has anyone done binary Tychonoff for formal topologies (Vickers/Coquand style — coverage relations on posets, point-free) in Lean 4, choice-free?
I've got a constructive version: formal topology + an operational compactness predicate + binary product, with Tychonoff by structural induction on cover derivations (following Vickers 2006). The axiom profile comes out [propext, Quot.sound] — no Classical.choice. There's also a constructive bridge to mathlib's Order.Frame.
I tried to find prior art and the closest I got is Ayberk Tosun's Agda locale theory (Stone/spectral, not Tychonoff). Did I miss anything in Lean?
Repo: github.com/inventor1975/VRCycle (under VRCycle/Topology/). Built with heavy AI assistance, for what it's worth. Mostly I just want to know if this already exists before I make any noise about it.

Cool!

We once did pointless Schemes https://github.com/spitters/pointless_scheme at https://conferences.au.dk/math-ai-workshop-2026 as a demo.
Mostly, because it would be the "right" way to do it in the style of Grothendieck. The LLM kept on getting confused by the pointwise versions of the theorems with the same name, but we got there in the end.

I also recently revisited our work on dualities in HoTT: https://arxiv.org/abs/1912.07339. The LLM is quite cable of doing that.
I've been experimenting with HoTT lean, and made a decent bit of progress, but programming new tactics seems to be the bottleneck.

Thanks for the reply. On pointless schemes — recognisable pain with the name collisions. I hit the same thing at the cover-relation level (our cov against mathlib's Order.Cover); resolved through namespace discipline and explicit constructors. As you say, got there in the end.
On HoTT in Lean — I'm an observer, not a participant. I work in classical Lean type theory without univalence. Programming tactics is a bottleneck for me too, but from the other side of the barricade — I have standard mathlib tactics available, the problem is more on the side of non-standard constructions than missing tooling.
In between, over the past couple of days I put together a blueprint of the whole VR cycle, so the connectivity from ∅ through all nine modules can be seen rather than read file by file: https://inventor1975.github.io/VRCycle/. Binary Tychonoff in point-free formulation is Chapter 9. Happy if you find it worth a look.
